Overview

Bern as a Business Centre

Bern is the seat of the Swiss federal government and parliament and the capital of the Canton of Bern, Switzerland's second most populous canton. The city itself is compact, with about 138,500 residents at the end of 2025 according to the Federal Statistical Office, but it is a significant employment centre: business statistics count more than 200,000 jobs within the city boundary in 2024, far more than it has residents. Much of that employment is in public administration, federal agencies, regulators and companies owned wholly or partly by the Confederation, together with health care, education, insurance and professional services. International bodies such as the Universal Postal Union are based here, and the cantonal administration and courts operate in both German and French.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Bern for reasons that differ from Zurich or Geneva. Suppliers and advisers to federal offices and state-linked enterprises must manage procurement integrity, conflicts of interest and reputational risk, and those organisations themselves commission internal inquiries when allegations arise. Companies facing Swiss regulatory or criminal proceedings engage with authorities headquartered in the city. Medtech, precision engineering and energy firms across the canton seek partners, acquisitions and investors whose backgrounds need checking. When disputes arise, the Commercial Court of the Canton of Bern and the cantonal Economic Crimes Court, both sitting in the city, are central forums, and research often needs to be conducted in both German and French.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Bern

01

Federal procurement and supplier integrity

Federal offices and state-linked enterprises in and around Bern buy IT, consulting, construction and defence-related services at scale. We research bidders, subcontractors and intermediaries, their ownership, management and previous disputes, and test for undisclosed relationships with officials that could create conflict of interest or procurement challenges.

02

Internal inquiries in public enterprises

Organisations owned by or closely linked to the Confederation face political and media scrutiny when allegations of misconduct, subsidy irregularities or conflicts of interest arise. We support their counsel with background research, document and timeline review and analysis of related companies, scoped to Swiss employment and data protection rules.

03

Regulatory and enforcement matters

Companies dealing with authorities based in Bern, including FINMA and the Office of the Attorney General, often need to understand counterparties, former employees or intermediaries connected to the matter. We assemble lawful public-record research on individuals and entities to support counsel's response and remediation.

04

Cantonal industry and acquisitions

The Canton of Bern hosts medtech, precision engineering, watchmaking and energy businesses, many family owned. Before an acquisition or partnership we use commercial register entries, official gazette notices, debt collection information obtained lawfully and German and French media to assess owners, management and disputes.

05

Asset research for Bern litigation

Claimants before the Commercial Court of the Canton of Bern or regional courts need to know what a counterparty holds and how it is structured. We map Swiss and foreign entities, signatories, real estate interests identifiable through counsel and connected persons, so counsel can plan attachment and enforcement.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Bern

Commercial Court of the Canton of Bern

The Canton of Bern is one of the few Swiss cantons with a specialised Commercial Court (Handelsgericht, Tribunal de commerce), which sits with the Supreme Court of the canton at Hochschulstrasse 17 in Bern. It hears commercial disputes between registered businesses and works in German and French. In 2024 the cantonal government consulted on allowing international disputes worth at least CHF 100,000 to be brought before it by agreement, with proceedings in English where needed. The status of that reform should be confirmed with Bernese counsel.

Supreme Court and Economic Crimes Court

The Supreme Court of the Canton of Bern (Obergericht) hears civil and criminal appeals and houses the cantonal supervisory authority for debt collection and bankruptcy. The cantonal Economic Crimes Court (Wirtschaftsstrafgericht), also in the city, tries complex economic crime cases at first instance. First-instance civil and criminal matters for the city go to the Regional Court Bern-Mittelland. Each court has German and French chanceries, which matters when reviewing judgments or filing translated evidence.

Commercial register and official gazette

Companies with their seat in the canton are entered in the commercial register kept by the Canton of Bern, searchable nationally through Zefix, with changes published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce. The federal commercial register office, which supervises cantonal registers, is part of the federal administration in Bern. Register extracts show purpose, capital, board members and signatories, while shareholders of a public limited company are not shown and need other lawful sources.

Federal authorities in the city

Bern hosts many federal authorities relevant to investigations, including FINMA, the Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland and the federal offices responsible for justice, procurement and economic affairs. Their published rulings, enforcement reports and registers of authorised institutions are useful sources when assessing financial counterparties. The Federal Supreme Court sits in Lausanne and the Federal Criminal Court in Bellinzona, so appeals and federal criminal trials take place outside Bern.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Bern

TDSC has no office in Bern and handles Bern matters from Nashville. We begin with the client and its Swiss counsel, agreeing whether the work supports a federal procurement relationship, an internal inquiry, a regulatory response, an acquisition in the canton or litigation before the Bernese courts. Research draws on the commercial register via Zefix, the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce, published cantonal and federal decisions, regulator publications and German and French-language media, read by native speakers. Swiss criminal law restricts acts on behalf of foreign states and economic intelligence gathering, so counsel reviews any evidence-gathering for foreign proceedings. Interviews or fieldwork are coordinated with appropriately qualified local professionals, within the Federal Act on Data Protection.

TDSC has no office in Bern. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Bern: Frequently Asked Questions

Which court hears a commercial dispute in Bern?

Disputes between businesses registered in the commercial register, where the conditions of the Swiss Civil Procedure Code are met, can go to the Commercial Court of the Canton of Bern. Other civil claims start at the Regional Court Bern-Mittelland. Appeals go to the cantonal Supreme Court and then the Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne. Bernese counsel advises on jurisdiction.

Can Bern's Commercial Court hear international cases in English?

The cantonal government consulted in 2024 on a reform that would let parties with at least one foreign domicile agree to bring disputes of CHF 100,000 or more before the Commercial Court, with English possible. We have not confirmed the reform's final form or commencement, so counsel should check its current status before drafting a jurisdiction clause.

How do you vet a supplier to a federal office?

We review the commercial register and gazette history, board members and signatories, related companies, published court decisions and procurement records, and German and French media. We look for undisclosed links to officials, prior exclusions or disputes, and financial distress indicators, then report findings with sources so the client can document its decision.

Can TDSC support an internal investigation at a Bern-based organisation?

Yes, as a consulting engagement led by the organisation's counsel. We help define scope, research individuals and entities from lawful public sources, review documents and chronology, and analyse related parties. Employee data is handled in line with Swiss data protection and employment law, and interviews are conducted by or with counsel.

Are there limits on gathering evidence in Bern for foreign proceedings?

Yes. The Swiss Criminal Code restricts unlawful acts on behalf of a foreign state and the disclosure of business secrets to foreign parties, which can affect evidence collection for foreign litigation or regulators. We therefore agree with Swiss counsel what information may be gathered and transferred, and use formal judicial assistance where it is required.
